title: Project Overview
description: Start with the README and the design source of truth to understand the game vision: a top-down pixel RPG about repairing an abandoned, season-organized region. IDEAS.md spells out the no-villains, adaptation-and-repair philosophy, the ambiguous Presences, the Trail of the Brother backstory, and the planned systems. AGENTS.md covers the code conventions and ReactiveUnity patterns you will see everywhere.

title: Boot Sequence
description: There is no classic entry point — Unity scenes bootstrap themselves. Bootstrapper.cs reads a BootstrapperConfig ScriptableObject to spawn persistent and per-scene prefabs, IntroManager resets player state and starts a fresh run, and StartGame launches the first level. LevelChanger, SmoothSceneManager, and SceneTransitionOverlay together handle scene loads with a fade overlay that survives scene unloads.

title: Core Systems: Clock, Save & Spawning
description: The two pillars everything else hangs off: GameClock (real time accumulated into game minutes/hours/days/seasons with tick events) and the JSON save pipeline. Persistence serializes with Newtonsoft, SaveData defines the ISaveable per-world-object contract, and SceneSaveLoadManager snapshots each scene's Impermanent container plus global player state. WorldState holds global water/rain/wind/temperature as static reactives that WorldStateByCalendar rewrites each day; SceneSpawner scatters world objects from tilemap markers on first visit.

title: Player: Movement & Interaction
description: How the player is driven. PlayerMovement reads input and derives an 8-way CompassDirection plus PlayerStates, with speeds tuned in PlayerMovementData and animation driven by PlayerAnimatorController. The grid-based interaction model lives in GridCursor (find targets under the cursor), PlayerCursor (the four directional cursors), InteractInput (resolves IInteractable targets), UseItem (routes items to world objects/tilemaps), and PlayerCrouch (stealth state).

title: Player: Inventory, Carry & Health
description: The resource model behind scarcity as a design lever. Inventory is a 10-slot ScriptableObject that persists to JSON, WeightyObjectStack + WeightyObjectType implement the weight-capped carry system with per-object weight and strength requirements, PlayerCarry handles pick-up/put-down, PlayerStrength and its tiers gate capacity, and PlayerWheelBarrow lets the player haul the whole barrow. PlayerHealth/PlayerHurtbox define damage absorption — taking a hit drops a carried item instead of health, tying combat risk back to the carry loop.

title: The Fishing Loop
description: Fishblitz began as a fishing game — this is the deepest core loop. Rod is the item that casts onto the Water tilemap and drives the state transition, FishingGame runs the timing minigame (rising cursor vs. trigger bars, configured per-fish in FishType), and FishBarTrigger is the hit-detection zone on the bar. MountedRod/PlacedMountedRod add the placed-rod variant on water tiles, and CaptureLog stamps catches with full game-clock timestamps for the journal.

title: The Birding Loop
description: The second primary loop, and a showcase for the project's steering AI. Binoculars flips the player into the birding state; BirdingGame is the frame-charge + tag minigame HUD, BirdingWinFrame the celebration overlay. On the world side, BirdBrain is a state machine spread across sibling files (flee, ground, perch, high/low flight), BirdSpeciesData are ScriptableObject species definitions, BirdSpawner places birds per season/week, and BirdFrightDetector triggers evasion when the player gets close.

title: Survival: Temperature, Wetness, Energy & Sleep
description: The living-limits simulation that makes the environment the antagonist. PlayerTemperatureManager drifts the player's dry temperature toward ambient (from OutsideTemperature, a singleton IHeatSource) and drops it while wet; PlayerDryingManager tracks the Wet/Dry state machine driven by rain. HeatSource/HeatSensitive/LocalHeatSource are the ambient-heat plumbing that fires and stoves plug into. PlayerEnergyManager is the central energy/diet state, Diet handles daily nutrition intake, and SleepMenu runs the end-of-day recovery sequence.

title: World Objects: Trees, Wood & Fire
description: The README's core loop in code: fell trees, split wood, dry it, burn it. TreePlant is the abstract choppable seasonal tree (Larch/Spruce and FallenLarch/FallenSpruce are concrete variants) and FallenTree the five-hit axe target. LarchStump is the firewood-crafting station that splits a dry log into firewood, Axe/DryLog are the tool and input items, and WoodRack dries wet logs over game minutes. Campfire and WoodStove run the fire lifecycle (Dead/Ready/Hot/Embers) that produces the warmth the survival step depends on.

title: Combat & Enemies
description: The weaponized conflict for the Way North. BasicWeapon defines RangedWeaponItem (fire-rate, clip, reload, projectile prefab) shared by bow and sling, BowChargeController choreographs the charge/crit window, and Projectile is the pooled round that deals damage. Damage flows through ContactHitbox → IHurtBox, with EnemyHealth/EnemyHurtbox on the receiving side. On the AI side, FlyingChaser wanders, sees the player with line-of-sight checks, then chases; ProjectileFiringEnemy keeps range and executes six shot patterns.

title: Narrative & Characters
description: Story is told through play, not interruption. Narrator is the scene-level overlay that queues brief pixel-text lines (unscaled time, so it works during pause). DialogueController renders speech bubbles, Gerard tracks the rescue arc as a three-stage ScriptableObject state machine, with UnconsciousGerard and ShedGerard as its two in-world variants, and IGiftable defines the gift-receiving contract (feeding the unconscious Gerard is how the player advances his story). Journal + JournalEntry render the Trail of the Brother notebook from the capture logs.

title: UI & Rendering
description: How the pixel-art look is produced. DynamicPixelPerfectCamera keeps an orthographic camera pixel-perfect (with CinemachinePixelSnap snapping to the grid during Finalize), PixelFont maps characters to glyph sprites, and PixelTextRenderer/PixelCanvasTextRenderer lay out crisp pixel text in world and screen space — everything from speech bubbles to the HUD uses them. TopRightHUD shows the clock/season from GameClock ticks, ItemSlot is the hotbar widget with drag-drop, and EnergyBar renders the energy meter.

title: The Way North Zone System
description: The procedural river progression mentioned in the design doc, implemented as a generated binary tree of biome nodes. TheWayNorth.cs is the manager — it builds a weighted tree from TheWayNorthConfig and BiomeConfig (weighted scene pools + fork scenes), tracks the traversal path with return links between exits and entrances, and persists the whole network. WeightedScene is the pickable scene entry, and the entrance/exit/spawn/transition components wire individual scenes into the graph.

title: Project Config & Next Steps
description: The dependency and input contract for the whole project, plus the forward-looking task list. manifest.json pins the stack (URP 17, Cinemachine, Input System 1.18, BlueOyster git package for ReactiveUnity + JSON saves) and fish blitz.inputactions defines the six input maps (Player, Birding, PlayerBarrowing, Combat, UI, Menu) the scripts reference. TODOS.md is the working task list — the practical starting point if you want to extend the game.
